title: War and Peace
objective: After this level you can explain how wars start and how they end.
summary: Clausewitz saw war as politics by other means. Rules on starting wars tightened from 1907 to 1945. An armistice stops a war; a peace treaty ends it.

cards.headline: On 11 November 1918, the guns fell silent. The war wasn't over yet.
cards.body: That day's armistice stopped the fighting on the Western Front, but the First World War formally ended only with the Treaty of Versailles, signed on 28 June 1919. Stopping a war and ending one turn out to be different steps. So is starting one.

cards.headline: Politics by other means
cards.body: Why do wars start? One classic answer comes from the Prussian general Carl von Clausewitz, whose book On War appeared in 1832, after his death. He argued that war is a continuation of state policy by other means. In his view, war isn't a break from politics: it's a tool governments pick up to pursue political goals.

events.label: Hague Convention III: no fighting without a declaration of war or an ultimatum
Kellogg-Briand Pact: war renounced as a tool of national policy, with no way to enforce it
UN Charter: members must not threaten or use force against other states
The Charter keeps the right of self-defence if an armed attack occurs

cards.headline: Stopping versus ending
cards.body: An armistice stops the fighting while the terms of peace are worked out. A peace treaty formally ends the war, as Versailles did after 1918's armistice. Sometimes the second step never comes: the Korean War armistice of 27 July 1953 stopped the fighting, but it was not a permanent peace treaty. Level 83's Kadesh tablet was the full kind: a peace treaty.

mascot.line: Armistice: the guns stop. Peace treaty: the argument is settled on paper.

cards.headline: War and peace: traced
learned: Clausewitz: war continues state policy by other means
The UN Charter bans force but keeps self-defence
An armistice stops fighting; a peace treaty ends a war

questions.prompt: What did the armistice of 11 November 1918 do?

options.label: It formally ended the First World War
options.rationale: The Treaty of Versailles did that, in 1919.

options.label: It started the First World War
options.rationale: It came at the end, not the start.

options.label: It stopped the fighting before a peace treaty

questions.explanation: The armistice stopped the fighting on the Western Front; the Treaty of Versailles formally ended the war in 1919.

questions.prompt: What was the main weakness of the 1928 Kellogg-Briand Pact?

options.label: Only two countries ever signed it
There was no way to enforce it
It required a declaration before every war
It banned self-defence against attack
options.rationale: It didn't; and the UN Charter keeps that right.

questions.explanation: The pact renounced war as a tool of national policy, but there was no way to enforce it, and it did not prevent World War II.

questions.prompt: War and peace chapter: how does Level 83's Kadesh tablet differ from the 1953 Korean War armistice?

options.label: Kadesh was a peace treaty; the 1953 deal only stopped the fighting
Kadesh only paused the fighting; Korea's was a full peace treaty
Both were declarations of war
options.rationale: Both came at the end of fighting, not the start.

options.label: Neither was ever put in writing

questions.explanation: The Kadesh treaty is the oldest known peace treaty; the Korean War armistice stopped the fighting but was not a permanent peace treaty.
